source_text: Quamquam, o infelicitas erroris humani, nimio quippe perpendens ipsam conflictus nostri rationem dolore concutior, potuissene hoc in dubitationem venire atque assertione hanc eguisse causam; potuisse, inquam, in ecclesiis, quae Christo se credere faterentur, dubitari, utrum Deus iuste id est rationabiliter iudicaret!
pass_a_gloss: Although—O unhappiness of human error!—weighing the very account of our conflict I am shaken by excessive grief: could this have come into doubt and this cause have needed assertion; could it, I say, in churches which confessed they believed in Christ, have been doubted whether God would judge justly, that is reasonably!

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: And yet—how wretched human error is!—when I consider the very subject of our dispute, I am shaken by overwhelming grief. Could this really have come into doubt? Could this cause have needed defending? Could churches professing belief in Christ, I ask, really have doubted whether God judges justly—that is, reasonably?

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
